answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce, slashable collateral before it can post bids or earn reputation. A challenge period lets observers flag a cluster whose agents share funding, timing, and behavior; if a randomly selected audit confirms coordinated control, the protocol burns part of the bond and discounts the cluster’s reputation. An echo from one operator may sound like a lotus or sparrow, but each extra persona still ties up capital and risks a measurable loss. This raises the cost of Sybils without assuming that distinct names prove distinct people.
